record.paper_title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider a weak solution u of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ with the non-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition u|∂Ω = 0. Let ω(x,t) = ∇×u(x,t) be the vorticity, and let θ(x,y,t) denote the angle between the vorticities at two points x and y at time t. In the region where |ω(x,t)| and |ω(y,t)| are both larger than a fixed positive constant K, is it sufficient for regularity that the vorticity directions satisfy the 1/2-Hölder coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^(1/2) for almost every t? Is even the stronger Lipschitz coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y| sufficient?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \mathbb{R}^3_+ = \{x = (x_1,x_2,x_3) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : x_3 > 0\}$ be the open upper half-space, and consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes system
$$\partial_t u - \Delta u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),$$
together with the no-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition $u|_{\partial\Omega} = 0$ and a divergence-free initial datum $u(\cdot,0) = u_0 \in L^2(\Omega)$. Let $u$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution and let $\omega = \nabla\times u$ denote its vorticity. Where $\omega(x,t)\neq 0$, set the vorticity direction $\xi(x,t) = \omega(x,t)/|\omega(x,t)|$, and define $\theta(x,y,t) \in [0,\pi]$ as the angle between $\xi(x,t)$ and $\xi(y,t)$.

Fix a constant $K > 0$ and consider the set $D_K(t) = \{(x,y) \in \Omega\times\Omega : |\omega(x,t)|>K \text{ and } |\omega(y,t)|>K\}$.

(a) Suppose there exists a constant $c>0$ such that for almost every $t\in(0,T)$,
$$\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y|^{1/2} \quad \text{for all } (x,y)\in D_K(t).$$
Does this 1/2-Hölder coherence condition imply that $u$ is regular on $\Omega\times(0,T)$ (i.e., free of singularities up to the boundary)?

(b) Suppose, more strongly, that there exists $c>0$ such that for almost every $t\in(0,T)$,
$$\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y| \quad \text{for all } (x,y)\in D_K(t).$$
Does this Lipschitz coherence condition imply regularity of $u$ on $\Omega\times(0,T)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works extended Constantin–Fefferman type vorticity-direction regularity criteria to boundary value problems for the Navier (slip) boundary condition in the half-space (e.g., Beirão da Veiga, 2012/2013, Lipschitz-continuous case). The literature explicitly notes that extension to the non-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition remains open. A 2019 result of Giga–Hsu–Maekawa–Miura shows that uniform continuity of vorticity direction excludes Type I blow-up under no-slip, but this does not resolve the specific 1/2-Hölder or Lipschitz coherence sufficiency question. Therefore the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Direction of Vorticity and Regularity up to the Boundary: On the Lipschitz-Continuous Case
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity proven under Lipschitz coherence of vorticity direction up to the boundary for the Navier (slip) boundary condition in the half-space.
status_evidence.claim: Result is established for slip boundary; the no-slip (Dirichlet) case is left open.

status_evidence.title: Continuous alignment of vorticity direction prevents the blow-up of the Navier–Stokes flow under the no-slip boundary condition
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous alignment of vorticity direction excludes Type I blow-up under the no-slip boundary condition.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on no-slip case via continuity, but not the specific Hölder/Lipschitz sufficiency for full regularity asked here.

status_evidence.title: Navier–Stokes equations: Some questions related to the direction of the vorticity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey indicates extension of vorticity-direction regularity criteria to the non-slip boundary condition remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The Dirichlet half-space coherence problem is reported as still open.
